idea_name: Continuous futures splice as sensing substrate
mechanism: Build a continuous futures OHLC series by splicing successive contracts from Market Watch either by simple addition at expiration or by addition-with-shift that replaces the last ~10 days of the expiring contract with the next contract, then run indicators on the synthetic daily series.
data_needed: SYMBOL_START_TIME/SYMBOL_EXPIRATION_TIME and full CopyRates history for each futures leg; ordered Market Watch list; PERIOD_D1 OHLC
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Ukrainian Stock index futures UX-9.13, UX-12.13, UX-3.14; PERIOD_D1 (demo on H1 chart for closed symbols)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a continuous front-month futures price path without broker-provided continuous symbols, so regime/vol sensors can run across roll gaps with an explicit splice policy.
quote: Fortunately, the history of the closed futures is always available in the terminal. Use this history to splice futures contracts in the terminal.

mechanism: Maintain a fan of short MA and EMA values on the latest two closes; ignore the raw close as noise; select MIN/MAX/MA/EMA according to prior cluster-filter direction so the smoother continues the assumed trend persistence, producing a non-redrawing stream estimate of the latent price/momentum path.
data_needed: Bar close stream; 2-period SMA and EMA; previous two CF outputs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol/timeframe closes; demo on Momentum (Blau relative) with GMomentum test modes
why_new_for_mis: MIS regime path can be estimated online by composing a vector of candidate smoothers and picking by persistence rules instead of a single lagging MA, without last-bar redraw.
quote: Cluster filters are convenient when analyzing non-stationary time series in real time, in other words, stream data. It means that these filters are of principal interest not for smoothing the already known time series values, but for getting the most probable smoothed values of the new data received in real time.

mechanism: Detrend and end-flatten a price window of length ~3*max_period, run Goertzel DFT over a min–max period band, form amplitude (optionally squared) and phase, then pick dominant cycle by peak amplitude or by cycle strength Amplitude/period; emit dominant period per bar for adaptive lookbacks.
data_needed: Price series (close); min_period (>=2), max_period; optional detrend/window/squared-amp flags; window size 3*max_period
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic price quotes; AdaptiveGARSI uses close; Maxper=72 Minper=5 defaults
why_new_for_mis: Provides a noisy-market alternative to MESA for sensing the prevailing cycle length as a regime feature and for driving adaptive indicator periods.
quote: According to Meyers the goertzel algorithm is able to outperform the MESA technique particularly when dealing with noisy signals, which is a common problem with financial time series.

idea_name: N-cycle Goertzel reconstructed wave with % peak/trough flips
mechanism: Sum the top N dominant Goertzel components into a filtered wave point; mark local peaks/troughs on that wave; flip Long/Short when the wave rises/falls more than pntup/pntdn percent from the last trough/peak (Meyers Adaptive 10 Cycle GDFT).
data_needed: Same Goertzel spectrum inputs; MaxCycles (e.g. 10); percent increase/decrease thresholds
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Price applied-price series; Maxper=72 Minper=5 MaxCycles=10
why_new_for_mis: Turns cycle decomposition into an explicit regime-change trigger on a noise-filtered reconstructed path rather than raw price crosses.
quote: He calls this strategy the Adaptive 10 Cycle Goertzel DFT System. Exact details about the strategy are available in the document. In brief the strategy uses the goertzel to extract the top ten dominant cycles from a moving window of price data , then uses these cycles to construct a new price curve.

mechanism: Build 17 predictors from 11 TTR indicators (ADX, aroon, CCI, Chaikin vol, CMO, MACD, OsMA, RSI, stoch, SMI, Yang–Zhang volatility), target ZigZag direction on median price, balance classes, spatialSign-normalize, unsupervised SAE layerwise then supervised DNN; decode with mean or 60/40 thresholds; optional ensemble average.
data_needed: OHLC (e.g. 4000 bars); ZigZag change; train/test split; SAE hidden sizes, LR, epochs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15 experiment; EURUSD M30 live SAE.model example
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a concrete deep-feature neural sensor over a mixed trend/oscillator/volatility panel with unsupervised pretrain and calibrated decode bands.
quote: At the first stage, information about internal structure of the input data is extracted from a large array of unformatted data with autoassociator through layer-by-layer unsupervised training. Then, using this information in a multi-layer neural network, it goes through supervised training by known methods using formatted data.

mechanism: Chart UI self-recovery/self-removal using OBJPROP_CREATETIME flags; no market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content after full read — terminal graphic-object protection only.
quote: This article, written in a simple language and containing easy examples, considers two variants of implementing program's response actions to the control panel's graphic objects being deleted or changed.

idea_name: CSV/INI text config for EA inputs
mechanism: Store rarely changed EA/indicator parameters in sandbox CSV text files with anchors; no market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: Configuration plumbing only; no regime/vol/liquidity/neural sensing after full read.
quote: When developing and using various trading tools, we sometimes come across the cases when standard means of inputs creation via extern and input modifiers are not sufficient enough.

idea_name: Higher-TF indicator values mapped by bar time with interpolation
mechanism: Compute classical indicators on a higher timeframe handle; on each lower-TF bar copy the HTF buffer by that bar’s open time; optionally linearly interpolate across the HTF bar’s constituent LTF bars so oscillators remain pattern-readable while still reflecting HTF state.
data_needed: HTF indicator handle (iMA/iMACD/…); CopyBuffer by datetime; CopyTime for HTF bar open; Interpolate flag
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic; examples M1–MN1, Elder three-screen stacks (e.g. M15-H1-H4, H1-H4-D1)
why_new_for_mis: Lets MIS fuse multi-timeframe regime state onto the working clock without naive period-scaling or waiting for HTF close alone.
quote: Therefore we need to bind the formation to the candlestick opening time. Let us implement this using the example of MA.

mechanism: CCanvas classes draw circular gauges and line graphs for values such as ADX/RSI/spread/drawdown; visualization layer, not a new sensing algorithm.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Examples on EURUSD various TFs; ACCOUNT_EQUITY/BALANCE for drawdown demo
why_new_for_mis: After full read this is custom-graphics chrome around existing values, not a new MIS sensor.
quote: The CCanvas custom graphics library allows developing custom non-standard indicators with infinite visualization capabilities.

idea_name: Naive Bayes fusion of independent indicator signals
mechanism: On each D1 bar estimate per-indicator hit probability P(H|E)=N_ok/N_total for fixed-horizon entries; combine independent signals via spam-filter-style product form P(H|ABC)=∏p_i/(∏p_i+∏(1-p_i)); trade only when ConsistentSignalNumber simultaneous signals agree; choose weakly correlated indicator sets (e.g. Stochastic, ATR/AC, Bollinger).
data_needed: Per-bar indicator signals; horizon TradeDuration bars; counts of hits vs total signals; optional custom iCustom indicators
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1, 2014–2017; Stochastic/MACD/Bollinger; TradeDuration=5 days default
why_new_for_mis: Formal probabilistic committee sensor that upgrades weak ~0.55 indicator edges into a joint posterior and enforces independence when packing features.
quote: To make the spam processing theory fully fit into our probabilistic trading theory, it is sufficient to replace the "spam" hypothesis with "successful trade", and the "word" event with "indicator's signal".

mechanism: Measure volatility with Chande Momentum Oscillator over a CMO period; use ABS(CMO) to scale the EMA smoothing factor F=2/(n+1) so averaging speed expands in volatile regimes and contracts when CMO is small.
data_needed: Price series; CMO period; EMA period; VIDYA recursion state
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD, AUDUSD; H1; 2016–2017 tests
why_new_for_mis: Directly couples a volatility oscillator into the smoother’s gain, yielding a volatility-aware trend path without a separate vol overlay.
quote: This is an EMA with its averaging period changing dynamically and depending on market volatility. Market volatility is measured by Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO).

idea_name: Bond-yield interest-rate differential and delta EMA
mechanism: Scrape US/DE/FR/IT 10y yields; form GDP-weighted EU composite f_EU=0.449*DE+0.315*FR+0.236*IT; IR differential = f_EU−f_US; delta = bar-to-bar change; optionally EMA(delta) with α=2/(n+1) as leading FX pressure sensor (update ~every 5 minutes).
data_needed: Web bond quotes (MarketWatch/WSJ API); GDP weights; local file for indicator readback; bar closes of differential
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD with US 10y T-note and DE/FR/IT 10y; hourly chart example; intraday basis-point moves
why_new_for_mis: Adds a fundamental cross-asset change sensor (rate-diff delta) that can lead FX regime shifts beyond pure price technicals.
quote: Bond yields are often a leading indicator of interest rates and of exchange rates. In the forex market, the metric that applies to a currency pair is the interest rate differential, especially the delta, or change in the interest rate differential, on various time frames.

idea_name: Candlestick pattern probability and efficiency sensors
mechanism: Classify bars into candle types (Marubozu/Doji/Spin/Hammer/Long/Short) via body/shadow ratios vs recent average body and local trend; detect classic or generated 1–3 candle patterns; over a sample range score post-pattern move categories with weights K1/K2/K3 and threshold points to emit Found, Coincidence%, Probability(up/down), and Efficiency coefficients.
data_needed: OHLC rates; trend_period; type coefficients; range_total; threshold_value; K1/K2/K3
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol/timeframe via library API; demo indicators CandleDetector/PatternDetector
why_new_for_mis: Turns candlestick patterns into quantitative occurrence/probability/efficiency features for regime and post-event directional sensing rather than binary pattern flags alone.

idea_name: Cluster filter of ahead-of-trend momentum errors
mechanism: Apply a more complex cluster filter to Momentum so impulsive overshoots in the trend direction are slowed while counter-trend noise produces a leading smoothed line; sensitivity control flattens false peaks without adding lag or redraw.
data_needed: Momentum (Blau relative or variants); cluster-filter sensitivity setting
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GMomentum test on chart quotes; impulse every 1024 bars in Test No.3
why_new_for_mis: Separates noise-induced lead from true impulse so MIS change detectors can use a de-noised momentum path that resists ahead-of-trend false breaks.
quote: Apparently, the momentum line can also make a wrong move in the other direction, i.e. unexpectedly shoot far in the direction of the trend, sometimes lingering far too long, even though the trend has already reversed. It would be logical if the filter could slow down such movements.

mechanism: Compute exponential smoothing factor from the current fractal dimension of the price series so the average tracks strong trends quickly and nearly freezes in consolidation, reducing false flat signals versus plain EMA.
data_needed: Price series; FRAMA period; fractal-dimension-based factor A(i)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same H1 FX basket as MA comparison (EURUSD etc.)
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a regime-aware smoother whose gain is explicitly tied to fractal dimension (trend vs consolidation), useful as a state feature.
quote: Here the smoothing factor is calculated on the basis of the current fractal dimension of price series. Indicator advantage is that it follows a strong trend and drastically slows down during consolidation periods.

mechanism: Compute Yang–Zhang volatility(OHLC,n,calc="yang.zhang",N=96) as one of 17 DNN inputs so the SAE/DNN direction model conditions on an OHLC-efficient volatility estimate alongside oscillators.
data_needed: OHLC; volatility lookback n (default 16); N=96 sessions factor
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15 panel in deep-net experiment
why_new_for_mis: Embeds a specific OHLC volatility estimator into a neural sensing stack rather than using close-to-close vol alone.
quote: Volatility (Yang and Zhang) - volatility(OHLC, n, calc="yang.zhang", N=96)- 1 out
